title: Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Adjudication payments total
sections.summary: By mid-2018, the adjudication process had facilitated payments of over $940 million.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As of mid-2018, the adjudication process has facilitated payments of over $940 million.

sections.label: Overseas prefabrication under SOP Act
sections.summary: Clause 3 covers overseas prefabrication works for local projects under the SOP Act, as up to 40% of Singapore projects may use such technologies by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Clause 3 will allow prefabrication works done overseas for local projects to be covered by the SOP Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: This is an important inclusion as our ITM envisages that by 2020, up to 40% of Singapore projects would incorporate productive construction technologies, and some of these may be sourced from overseas by Singapore builders.

sections.label: Adjudicators respect suspension clauses
sections.summary: Clause 3 requires adjudicators to respect contract clauses on suspension of payment for terminated contracts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: As such, clause 3 will require adjudicators to respect the contract clauses on suspension of payment for terminated contracts.

sections.label: Adjudication case took 129 days
sections.summary: One adjudication case took 129 days because the adjudicator needed more time for prolongation cost claims, 70% of the total claimed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: For example, one adjudication case took 129 days as the adjudicator needed more time to go through the claims for prolongation costs, which made up 70% of the total claimed amount.

sections.label: Payment claim served early valid
sections.summary: Clause 5 provides that a payment claim is valid even if served before the date or period specified in the contract.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: To address this, clause 5 will provide that the payment claim will be valid even if it is served before the date or the period specified in the contract.

sections.label: Repeating payment claims allowed
sections.summary: Clause 5 clarifies that claimants may repeat a payment claim even without additional work, goods or services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Clause 5 will clarify that claimants are allowed to repeat a payment claim even without additional work done or goods or services supplied.

sections.label: Belated objections disregarded by adjudicators
sections.summary: Clauses 9, 11, 14 and 17 make clear that belated objections by respondents will be disregarded unless they prove the objections could not have been made known earlier.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: To that end, clauses 9, 11, 14 and 17 will make clear that any belated objections by respondents will be disregarded by adjudicators or the Courts, unless respondents can prove that their objections could not have been made known earlier.

sections.label: Minimum interest rate for late payments
sections.summary: Clause 4 sets a minimum interest rate based on the rate under the Supreme Court of Judicature Act, currently 5.33%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Such a low interest rate is ineffective in deterring late payments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: So, clause 4 will set a minimum interest rate based on the rate specified under the Supreme Court of Judicature Act, which currently stands at 5.33%.

sections.label: Grounds to set aside adjudication determination
sections.summary: Clause 17 specifies a non-exhaustive list of grounds for setting aside an adjudication determination, such as a repeated claim already adjudicated on its merits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: In this regard, clause 17 will specify a non-exhaustive list of grounds on which parties can commence proceedings to set aside the adjudication determination.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: For example, if a claimant repeats a claim that is subsequently found to have already been adjudicated on its merits, the determination for the repeated claim may be set aside.

sections.label: Amendments ensure prompt payment practices
sections.summary: The amendments are believed to keep the Act ensuring prompt payment practices in the construction industry and help firms thrive in domestic and overseas markets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: With these amendments, we believe that the Act will continue to ensure prompt payment practices in our construction industry, and also put our firms in a better position to thrive in both domestic and overseas markets.

sections.label: Adjudicators consider supported damage items
sections.summary: New section 19(5A) clarifies that adjudicators can only consider damage, loss or expense items supported by documents showing party agreement on the amount or a certificate certifying the claim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, the new section 19(5A) clarifies that adjudicators can only consider damage, loss or expense items which are supported by documents showing agreement between parties on the amount or a certificate certifying the claim issued under the contract.

sections.label: Fresh objections when setting aside determination
sections.summary: New section 19(6A) clarifies a respondent setting aside an adjudication determination can only raise a fresh objection if new circumstances arose, the objections could not have been made earlier, or there was a patent error.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, the new section 19(6A) clarifies that a respondent setting aside the adjudication determination can only raise a fresh objection to the payment claim if: one, new circumstances had arisen; two, the objections could not have been made earlier because the respondent could not have known of these reasons; or three, there was a patent error.

sections.label: Subcontractors' fear of losing jobs
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes amendments to help subcontractors' cash flow, but says many subcontractors fear losing jobs and only resort to law last.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, I welcome the amendments which will help the subcontractors enhance their cash flow and minimise losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, many subcontractors had told me that they are likely to continue to suffer in silence and resort to the law only as a last resort as they are afraid to lose jobs from main contractors.

sections.label: Project funds diverted by owners
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to strengthen regulations so funds for a specific project cannot be diverted for other uses when owners face financial difficulty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Occasionally, the owner runs into financial difficulty halfway through the construction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I strongly urge the Ministry to further strengthen the regulations to ensure that the funds for a specific project are not allowed to be diverted for other uses.

sections.label: Replacement of review adjudicators
sections.summary: The amendments clarify that when most review adjudicators are replaced, a remaining original adjudicator can brief the new ones without restarting the review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The amendments before the House provide clarity in situations where any of the review adjudicators are replaced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In situations where the majority of review adjudicators are replaced, the remaining adjudicator that was involved from the onset can apprise the new adjudicators of the case, and there would be no need to start the adjudication review afresh.

sections.label: Panel of review adjudicators appointments
sections.summary: Appointing a panel of review adjudicators is uncommon, occurring only when the adjudicated amount exceeds the response amount by $1 million or more, with 15 appointments since 2005.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: I would also like to highlight that the appointment of a panel of review adjudicators is not common.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: This happens only when the adjudicated amount exceeds the response amount by $1 million or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As such, we note that there have only been 15 such appointments since the introduction of the SOP Act in 2005.

sections.label: Project bank accounts study
sections.summary: The Ministry will study project bank accounts and monitor Queensland's model, which requires head contractors to establish them for government building projects worth $1 million to $10 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: One possible approach would have been to require the developer of a project to make payments into a project bank account, which parties can then draw down from for work done or goods supplied to the project.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: In October last year, Queensland amended its equivalent of the SOP Act to require head contractors to establish project bank accounts for government building projects worth between $1 million and $10 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: As such a move would affect many industry stakeholders and increase the administrative burden on companies, we will take more time to carefully study this approach and to monitor the effectiveness of Queensland’s model before deciding on the next steps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: By taking on feedback and views from the industry players, the revised SOP Act should help to create a more conducive operating environment for all parties in the construction industry.
